title: Expectation under a mixture
statement: Let $\Omega$ and $\Lambda$ be finite sets, let $P$ be a probability distribution on $\Omega$, and for each $x\in\Omega$ let $Q_x$ be a probability distribution on $\Lambda$. For any function $f:\Lambda\to\mathbb{R}$, its expectation under the distribution obtained by first sampling from $P$ and then from $Q_x$ is the expectation under $P$ of the conditional expectation under $Q_x$; that is, $\mathbb{E}_{x\sim P,\,y\sim Q_x}[f(y)]=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim P}[\mathbb{E}_{y\sim Q_x}[f(y)]]$.
hypotheses_covered: $Q_x$ is a probability distribution on $\Lambda$ for each $x\in\Omega$
